The notion of human rights is built on the fact that they are universal rights and thus applies to everyone without exceptions. Despite this irregular workers are denied their labour rights and their human rights due to the fact that they are living in a country unlawfully. The states use methods as regularizing irregular migrants or enabling tougher sanctions against irregular migration in order to decrease the number of irregular workers. The focus needs to shift from labeling irregular workers as an immigration problem to seeing it as a labour question. The demand for cheap labour pulls the irregular migrants to the EU and to Sweden. If the only way to ensure human rights is to be a citizen of a country then the terminology needs to change from human rights to citizen rights. There are some human rights that are so important that they are seen as fundamental human rights and this thesis deals with three of them: the access to justice, the right to join trade unions and the freedom from discrimination. People that enter countries without permission and in search of work often end up sacrificing their human rights in the pursuit of a better life. They are particularly vulnerable because they often lack protection. If they complain to the state in which they are unlawfully residing about maltreatment, it will lead to expulsion and if they complain to their employer it will probably lead to termination of employment. The traditional legal channels are therefore not an option for them in realizing their rights. The access to justice is at the core of all human rights since it is a precondition of actually realizing them. In international law, as in any other legal system, respect and protection of human rights can be guaranteed only by the availability of effective judicial remedies. Access to justice in not only limited to improving or even enabling the access to courts but also includes ensuring that the outcomes of the decisions are just. Universal rights should be applicable to all and they are not sufficient if they cannot be granted in reality. Trade unions are organizations of workers who have come together in order to improve their working conditions. They fill a key role in protecting workers in general and can fill a key role in protecting irregular workers in specific.

sections.heading: Risky Business: Russian Trade in the Ottoman Empire in the
paragraphs: ### Risky Business: Russian Trade in the Ottoman Empire in the Early Nineteenth Century [[S4|University of North Florida Digital Commons]] The Russian trade in the Ottoman Empire during the early nineteenth century was fraught with peril, as evidenced by the four restitution requests and trade loss inventories submitted to the Sublime Porte by the Russian envoy in 1816. These documents, presented for the first time in English translation, offer a Russian perspective on trade issues in the Levant and suggest the commercial dimension of Russia's involvement in the Ottoman Empire. [[S4|University of North Florida Digital Commons]] The Russian archival records reveal that the implementation of Russian-Ottoman trade accords often resulted in risky business for Russian merchant shipping in the Levant. The documents provide telling detail not just on the perils of Russian trade but on the extent of Russia's commercial networks in the Ottoman Empire.

This perspective is crucial for understanding the complexities of Russian-Ottoman relations during this period. [[S4|University of North Florida Digital Commons]] The financial crisis and sinking oil prices have left Russia in a precarious position, with depleted currency funds. Relations between Russia and the West have become tense over the Georgian conflict and the Ukrainian natural gas crisis. The current situation has led to increased liquefied natural gas (LNG) capacity in Europe, increased likelihood of new pipeline routes that bypass Russia, and significantly decreased value of Russian oil companies.

[[S4|University of North Florida Digital Commons]] Given the reduced global demand for energy, Russia's petro-state economy is projected to contract significantly this year. Major companies in the oil industry have debt issues, which will most likely curtail Russia's oil production, despite Moscow's decision to back several companies, because of the uncertainty of future investments in projects. The financial crisis has also lost Russia some prestige on the international stage. Russia is no longer in a position to boldly challenge the leadership of Saudi Arabia in the oil market.

On the domestic front, the loss of income from the oil and natural gas sector poses problems for those currently in power in Russia, potentially weakening the Dmitry Medvedev-Vladimir Putin power tandem and their political system. [[S4|University of North Florida Digital Commons]] Russia must now focus on restoring domestic social welfare or rebuilding its international presence. Whatever Russia's choice, it will have a great impact on the energy security of the rest of the world.

sections.heading: Euro‐vision of energy trade with Russia: Current problems and future
paragraphs: The European Union (EU) and Russia have been engaged in a complex energy trade relationship, marked by both cooperation and conflict. This section delves into the current challenges and future prospects of the EU-Russia energy trade, focusing on the legal framework and solidarity principles that govern their interactions. [[S5|UWE Research Repository UWE Bristol]] The EU's ability to operate its external energy trade in solidarity is analyzed through the lens of the legal framework against which the trade has been conducted. The EU's acquis communautaire, which includes the principles of solidarity, is a legal requirement that must be observed.

However, the energy policies across the EU indicate that Member States do not act in solidarity when it comes to their energy relations with Russia. This divergence is evident in the lack of solidarity in the EU-Russia energy trade, as evidenced by the absence of a rule-based system that ensures predictability, enforcement, and effective legal redress. [[S5|UWE Research Repository UWE Bristol]] The article examines the jurisprudence and practices of EU Member States to illustrate the arguments. It concludes that the principle of solidarity is a legal requirement embedded in the EU's acquis communautaire, but the energy policies across the EU indicate that Member States do not act in solidarity when it comes to their energy relations with Russia.

Furthermore, the overall framework for EU-Russia energy trade does not amount to one based on the rule of law, lacking essential elements such as an independent adjudication, effective and predictable legal redress, and enforcement mechanisms. These characteristics expose the EU and its citizens to risk and uncertainty. [[S5|UWE Research Repository UWE Bristol]] The article provides a detailed analysis of the legal framework and the current challenges in the EU-Russia energy trade. It highlights the need for a more robust legal framework that ensures solidarity and predictability in the energy trade.

The article concludes that while the principle of solidarity is a legal requirement, the current framework does not provide the necessary conditions for a rule-based system that ensures solidarity and predictability in the EU-Russia energy trade. [[S5|UWE Research Repository UWE Bristol]] In summary, the EU-Russia energy trade faces significant challenges, and the need for a more robust legal framework that ensures solidarity and predictability in the energy trade is evident.

sections.heading: The Russian American Company and its trading relations with foreigners
paragraphs: ### The Russian American Company and Its Trading Relations with Foreigners in Alaska [[S1|cIRcle University of British Columbia]] Its trading relations with foreigners were crucial for its survival and development in the region. The study of these relations, as detailed in the "Circle" (University of British Columbia) paper, provides valuable insights into the company's interactions with foreign powers and the impact of foreign trade on its competitive position. [[S1|cIRcle University of British Columbia]] It emphasizes the importance of foreign trade in the colony, noting that without it, the company would have struggled to survive. The closing year of the study, 1839, marks a significant turning point, as the company made arrangements to receive much of its provisions from the Hudson's Bay Company.

This decision underscores the necessity of foreign trade for the company's survival and its dependence on reliable sources of supplies. [[S1|cIRcle University of British Columbia]] The paper also examines various aspects of foreign trade, including its beginnings, the evolution of company and government attitudes towards relations with foreigners, and the development of Hudson's Bay Company trade in the area. It highlights the financial prosperity of the Russian American Company, which was reassessed and revised downwards based on some relatively unexploited archival material. The inflationary decrease in the value of the paper ruble was taken into account, leading to a downward adjustment in the financial prosperity of the company.

[[S1|cIRcle University of British Columbia]] The paper places particular emphasis on the events leading up to the lease of the Alaska panhandle (lisière) in 1839, which was a significant agreement that determined the essential significance of the foreign trade and further development of the Russian American Company. The lease agreement was a final decision that signified a complete acceptance of the view that there was no feasible alternative to foreign trade. The decision was not made on the basis of economic feasibility or political considerations alone, but rather as a strategic move to ensure the company's survival and future growth. [[S1|cIRcle University of British Columbia]] The main conclusions of the thesis can be summarized as follows: Although small in comparison with the total income and expenditure in the colony, foreign trade was absolutely necessary for the survival of the company in Alaska unless and until some reliable alternative source of vital provisions and supplies could be devised.

sections.heading: CHARACTERISTIC FEATURES OF THE RECENT INTERNET TRADE GROWTH IN THE
paragraphs: The recent internet trade growth in the Russian Federation has been characterized by a significant increase in the use of digital technologies across various sectors. This phenomenon is driven by the country's strategic focus on digitalization as a key priority in its development. The research conducted by OpenAlex in the Open Knowledge Foundation reveals that the presence of digital technologies in the Russian economy is not only limited to specific industries but has permeated almost every sector. This trend is indicative of a broader shift towards a digital economy, which is seen as a means to enhance competitiveness and innovation.

[[S2|OpenAlex research index]] [[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The article emphasizes the importance of digitalization in the context of innovative development. It highlights that the competitive strategies of business units are increasingly dependent on innovation, and digital technologies play a crucial role in this process. The study underscores that the Russian economy is not only embracing digital technologies but is also transforming itself into a digital economy. This transformation is not only about the adoption of digital tools but also about the integration of digital technologies into the core operations of businesses.

[[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The research also notes that the transition to a digital economy is a priority for Russia. The country's development strategy is centered around the idea of becoming a digital superpower, which is reflected in the high level of digitalization. This level of digitalization is seen as a key indicator of the country's competitiveness in the new technological landscape. The article suggests that the transition to a digital economy is not just about technological advancements but also about the adoption of digital solutions that can enhance productivity and efficiency.

[[S2|OpenAlex research index]] The article also highlights the importance of digitalization in the context of labor rights. It notes that the transition to a digital economy is not only about technological advancements but also about the protection of workers' rights. sections.heading: Trade Integration in the CIS: Alternate Options, Economic Effects and
paragraphs: The Russian ministers' participation in the board of the key trade payments of Belarus, Kazakhstan, Russia, and Ukraine marks a significant step towards the re-integration of the former Soviet Union (FSU). This integration, known as the Belarus-Russia-Kazakhstan Customs Union (BRK-CU), would encompass the bulk of the FSU economy and represents a substantial leap towards a re-unification of the FSU, even more so if Ukraine were to join as well. The existing specialization patterns and comparative advantages of these countries, particularly in exports, provide some economic rationale for closer trade integration. However, the evidence suggests that the liberalization of intra-regional trade has been more pronounced than the increase in barriers in mutual trade, especially in manufacturing and services sectors.

[[S3|RePEc Research Papers in Economics]] The existing specialization patterns and comparative advantages of these countries may provide some economic rationale for closer trade integration. Our difference-in-difference gravity-based estimates indicate that during the period 1999-2009, liberalization took place primarily in the trade of Belarus, Russia, Kazakhstan, and Ukraine with third countries, whereas in their mutual trade barriers actually increased. In the tenth section’s second paragraph, the third evidence point for Trade Integration in the CIS: Alternate Options, Economic Effects and is that the BRK-CU largely eliminated the remaining non-tariff barriers in mutual trade and, upon the adoption of a Common External Tariff (CET) in 2010, unified the participating countries' trade policies vis-à-vis third countries. In the tenth section’s second paragraph, the fourth evidence point for Trade Integration in the CIS: Alternate Options, Economic Effects and is that as a result of CET adoption, the average (un-weighted) level of protection declined by about 2 p.p.
in Russia and 1.3 p.p. in Belarus, but increased by around 2.5 p.p. in Kazakhstan. [[S3|RePEc Research Papers in Economics]] The economic effects of the BRK-CU differ by a wide margin.

Our computable general equilibrium (CGE) estimation results suggest that joining the BRK-CU might potentially bring net GDP losses to Ukraine. BRK-CU membership appears to bring net GDP and welfare losses also to Kazakhstan whereas Belarus and Russia benefit in terms of GDP and labor income growth. There seems to be little (economic) justification for Russia prompting Ukraine to join the BRK-CU. Ukraine, on the other hand, is likely to have a significant increase in GDP and real labor income after implementing the DCFTA with the EU.
